page: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v6 is an x86_64 general purpose virtual machine powered by dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processors operating at 3.7 GHz under the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The configuration provides 96 vCPUs derived from 48 physical cores with two threads per core. Memory capacity is provisioned at 384 GB, preserving a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per virtual processor. The processor architecture includes advanced vector and cryptographic instruction sets, such as AVX-512 with VNNI and BF16, AES, and SHA_NI. The instance does not feature discrete GPU accelerators.

A primary hardware differentiator is the inclusion of 5669 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD storage, providing substantial high-speed temporary disk volume. Benchmark metrics reveal strong overall computational performance: stress-ng multi-core testing records top-tier results that place the instance in the upper decile, supported by strong single-core scores. In-memory data store throughput is also robust, with the platform logging 113.08 million Redis SET operations per second.

From an infrastructure perspective, bundling over 5.6 TB of direct-attached NVMe storage delivers high resource density for disk-intensive scratch operations without requiring additional attached storage arrays. Tradeoffs include the absence of hardware accelerators and reliance on ephemeral local disks for storage performance. Given these hardware and benchmark attributes, Microsoft Azure D96ads_v6 is appropriate for high-concurrency relational database servers, Redis caching clusters, ETL data transformation jobs, and heavily parallel enterprise application backends.
description: Microsoft Azure D96ads_v6 is a general purpose virtual machine built on AMD EPYC 9V74 processors running at 3.7 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. The system provisions 96 dedicated vCPUs across 48 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading and 384 GB of system RAM, maintaining a balanced 1:4 core-to-memory ratio. Hardware support includes AVX-512 extensions with BF16 and VNNI, while graphical acceleration is absent. Storage is supported by 5669 GB of bundled local NVMe SSD media. In benchmark evaluations, the server achieves top-tier multi-core compute throughput on stress-ng and strong single-core performance. Additionally, it achieves 113.08 million operations per second on Redis SET benchmarks. The combination of high parallel execution capacity and fast local NVMe storage provides qualitative efficiency for large relational database engines, high-throughput caching tiers, enterprise ETL pipelines, and multi-threaded data processing workloads.
